bib.title: Effective Long-Context Scaling of Foundation Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Appendix B proof read in outline. Figures 3, 7, 9 are images (values not in text).

question: How can open long-context LLMs with effective windows up to 32,768 tokens be built from Llama 2, and which design choices (positional encoding, data mix, curriculum, instruction data) matter?
hypothesis: Long-context capability can be learned by continually pretraining a short-context model, and a RoPE decay fix is needed for attending to distant tokens.
contributions: Open series of long-context LLMs (7B-70B) continually pretrained from Llama 2 on 400B tokens, up to 32,768 tokens
Power-law scaling of loss with context length
Cheap instruction tuning without human-annotated long data, 70B beats gpt-3.5-turbo-16k on many long tasks
Ablations of positional encoding, data mix, training curriculum

method.summary: Continually pretrain Llama 2 (7B/13B/34B/70B) for 400B tokens/100,000 steps on longer sequences with RoPE base frequency raised from 10,000 to 500,000 and an upsampled long-text data mix, then instruction-tune on Llama 2 Chat RLHF data plus self-instruct long QA data generated by Llama 2 Chat. Evaluate on short benchmarks, long QA/summarization benchmarks, ZeroSCROLLS, L-Eval, human preference and safety.

metrics.name: Validation loss/perplexity

results.claim: Larger models fit a larger power-law exponent beta in validation loss vs context length; 70B has beta 0.51.
results.setup: Llama 2 Long 70B, validation loss L(c)=(alpha/c)^beta+gamma, contexts up to 32,768 tokens; 7B: 25.4/0.45/1.56, 13B: 19.5/0.48/1.45, 34B: 17.7/0.50/1.41, 70B: 17.9/0.51/1.35 (alpha/beta/gamma)
results.quote: Larger models can leverage the contexts more effectively, indicated by the larger β value of the curves.

results.claim: Doubling context of the 70B model reduces the reducible loss by about 0.7x, with diminishing returns up to 32,768 tokens.
results.setup: 70B model, language modelling loss, power-law fit
results.quote: if we double the context length, we can expect the loss to be reduced by a factor of 2−β ≈0.7 plus a model specific constant (1 −2−β) · γ.

results.claim: Llama 2 Long 70B scores 79.7 EM on QuALITY (2-shot) vs 53.0 for Llama 2 70B, prompts up to 16,384 tokens.
results.setup: Pretrained models, 2-shot, validation sets, max prompt 16,384 tokens, prompt '{CONTEXT} Q: {QUESTION}, A:'
results.table: Table 3, row LLAMA 2 LONG 70B, column QuALITY EM (2-shot)

results.claim: Llama 2 Long 70B chat beats gpt-3.5-turbo-16k on 7 of 10 ZeroSCROLLS tasks, with avg 37.7 vs 36.7.
results.setup: Instruction-tuned 70B, benchmark's own prompts/truncation/max generation lengths
results.quote: our 70B chat model is able to outperform gpt-3.5-turbo-16k on 7 out of the 10 tasks
results.table: Table 4, row LLAMA 2 LONG CHAT 70B vs GPT-3.5-turbo-16k, column Avg

results.claim: Task results improve monotonically with maximum input length (4,096 to 16,384); QMSum ROUGE-geo 10.9 to 16.5.
results.setup: Llama 2 Long 70B (inferred from Table 3 values), max input 4,096/8,192/12,288/16,384, read from Fig 2
results.note: Fig 2 values read from the text-extracted figure labels; NarrativeQA 27.5->30.9, Qasper 28.9->35.7, QuALITY 63.9->79.7 (80.3 at 8k is above 79.7 at 16k, so not strictly monotone for QuALITY as printed)
results.quote: we first show in Figure 2 that the results on each long task improve monotonically as we increase the context lengths

results.claim: With unmodified RoPE, the model could not attend beyond about 4,000-6,000 tokens even after long continual pretraining.
results.quote: our model was unable to effectively attend beyond 4, 000 - 6, 000 tokens even after extensive long-context continual pretraining

results.claim: Raising RoPE base frequency from 10,000 to 500,000 (ABF) is the only variant that keeps first-sentence retrieval up to the full 32,768 context.
results.setup: 7B continued from Llama 2 with 80B tokens in 32,768-token sequences; variants RoPE, PI, ABF, xPos ABF
results.quote: increasing the “base frequency b” of ROPE from 10, 000 to 500, 000

results.claim: Books validation perplexity at 32,768 tokens: RoPE ABF 6.323 vs RoPE 6.548.
results.table: Table 5, row ROPE ABF, column Books

results.claim: Removing most long text from the pretraining mix keeps most of the gain; quality not length drives it (QuALITY +67.1% vs +75.5% full mix vs +60.3% Llama 2 mix).
results.metric: QuALITY relative improvement, remove long text
results.table: Table 7, row - remove long text data, column Quality ΔEM

results.claim: Continual pretraining from a 4k model saves about 40% FLOPs vs 32k from scratch with almost no performance loss.
results.setup: 7B, 4k->32k switch at 20/40/80% of training; 4M tokens per gradient update; FLOPs 3.783e22 scratch vs 3.026e22 at 40% (not exactly 40% for each row)
results.quote: continual pretraining from short context models can easily save around 40% FLOPs while imposing almost no loss on performance
results.table: Table 10, rows 32k from scratch vs 4k→32k @ 40%, column FLOPs

results.claim: Adding LM loss on long input prompts during self-instruct finetuning raises Qasper from 35.7 to 38.9 and QuALITY from 59.3 to 77.3.

results.table: Table 9, row RLHF V5 mix self-inst with LM loss, column Qasper

results.claim: Attention matrix cost only becomes the compute bottleneck for the 70B (h=8192) above 49,152 tokens.

limits: No code, weights or data release stated; pretraining data mix composition, batch size, optimizer, hardware, instruction-tuning hyperparameters and self-instruct data size are not given.
Authors concede: not finetuned for long-form output tasks such as creative writing; alignment (RLHF) for long contexts is expensive.
Tokenizer yields about 10% more tokens than GPT-3.5 and handles whitespace poorly, so 32,768 tokens hold fewer words.
Hallucination is likely more pronounced for long-context models.
Automatic metrics for summarization are weak, truncation may remove needed information, and leakage in proprietary models cannot be ruled out.
Safety evaluation covers three benchmarks plus informal red teaming; no long-context safety benchmark exists.
Scaling-law fit covers contexts up to 32,768 only; ablations are at 7B.
Single runs; no seeds or variance for benchmark numbers.
Dated: 2023 models and baselines (Llama 2, GPT-3.5-16k, Claude 1/2).
